stem: A middle school faculty surveyed students to determine interest in an after-school chess club. Of the 100 students who were selected at random from all students in the school, 32% expressed interest in the club. Based on the sample mean and the margin of error, the faculty expects that between 24% and 40% of all students in the school would express interest in the club. What is the margin of error?
rationale:
Choice B is correct. It's given that of the 100 students who were selected at random from all students in the school, 32% expressed interest in the club. It's also given that based on the sample mean and the margin of error, the faculty expects that between 24% and 40% of all students in the school would express interest in the club. These values are calculated by subtracting the margin of error from 32% to get the lower bound, 24%, and by adding the margin of error to 32% to get the upper bound, 40%. It follows that the margin of error can be calculated as the difference between 32% and 24% or between 40% and 32%. The difference between 32% and 24% is 32-24%, or 8%.

Choice A is incorrect and may result from conceptual or calculation errors.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the difference between 40% and 24%, not the difference between 32% and 24% or between 40% and 32%.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the percentage of the students selected at random who expressed interest in the club, not the margin of error.
